text:
maria: quick heads-up — I ran a mixed-precision pass on mistral-8b (fp8 primary, int4 fallback) against our long-seq suite and saw a 12-18% latency regression past seq=1024 vs baseline int8. attaching profiler snippet.

perf-ci-bot: perf run 2063004321 on mrsl-8b-mixed-v2
```
> seq_len=2048, batch=1
> kernel_selector: chosen path=matmul_int4_block128 -> 85% of runtime
> kv_cache: spill_count=7, avg_spill_size=64KB
> memcpy_h2d: +2.1ms per step
> total_p99=152ms (baseline int8 p99=129ms)
```

tao: hm. that kernel_selector line is suspicious — block128 int4 matmul has lower FLOPs per launch but higher kernel-launch overhead. if seq grows, we call kernels more often and overhead adds up.

alex: also note kv_cache spill_count=7. when the kv cache spills we see extra memcpy + kernel fallback to smaller tile kernels. combined effect explains the spike. iirc we saw similar behavior with the fp8 calibration that changes kv-sizes.

maria: right. i toggled calibration sampling from 5%->1% (coarser) and the selector moved to fp8_matmul_block256 for shorter prefixes but still flips to int4 path around 900 tokens.

tao: can you paste the quant profile you used? curious about the per-layer dtype mapping.

maria: pasted below (trimmed):
```
{
  "model": "mistral-8b",
  "layers": {
    "0-10": "fp8",
    "11-40": "int8",
    "41-60": "int4",
    "61-127": "int8"
  },
  "kv_cache_policy": "dynamic_spill:threshold=512KB",
  "calibration": "sampling=0.01,seed=42"
}
```

alex: that dynamic_spill threshold looks low for our runtime. it will trigger throttled memcpy earlier. try bumping threshold to 2MB and re-run. also set kernel_selector hysteresis so we don't oscillate between block128/block256 mid-request.

maria: noted — i'll try threshold=2MB and add hysteresis=0.15 (15% throughput tolerance).

ops-ryan: FYI if this needs infra changes (more reserved device memory to raise kv threshold) ping me. we can reserve a small burst pool on the dedicated cluster for repro.

tao: one more thought — calibration noise can make certain layers prefer int4 which reduces compute but increases indexing cost for kv lookups (different kernel path). calibration->quality tradeoff might be hiding as perf regressions. we should run quality evals alongside perf.

maria: agreed. plan: 1) bump kv threshold to 2MB + add selector hysteresis; 2) re-run perf + quality on our eval set; 3) if improved, push a new profile to /configs/quant/mistral/mistral-8b-mixed-v3.json and open a canary for dedicated.

alex: sg. if you want i can add a short script to automate profiling and attach a flamegraph to the PR. would help reviewers spot memcpy spikes.

maria: please do. tagging @alex for the script. thanks! :thumbsup:
